_why: The painted surface of all 72 surfaces — the sixteen tabs, Home and the Workflow canvas, in four palettes — read by `npm run check:snapshot` (`scripts/snapshot_surfaces.mjs`). Each entry records where the header, activity rail, main pane and its first panel sit, how many buttons, inputs, links, headings, canvases and tables the surface has, and the resolved colours, type and palette tokens. It is **not a pixel diff**: the runner is Linux and the person writing this is on a Mac, and a baseline whose antialiasing does not survive the trip is a gate people learn to skip. Box numbers are compared with a 2 px tolerance, so subpixel rounding is not a finding; counts and resolved styles are exact. The Links tab draws its tables from `app/src/data/linkHistoryData.ts`, which the weekly sweep regenerates: a data refresh that changes a host or run count moves that surface and is a re-record too (`--record --tab tab-links` records all four palettes). The Workflow surface records each card’s box, every port dot, each arrow’s path and the label, kind chip and remove button that hang from its half-way point, and the named frame that groups the cards with its chip — seeded through the panel’s own blank/code/branch/condition path and its Group gesture so every palette records the same authored diagram. Re-record with `npm run check:snapshot -- --record` when a change to the screen is intended, and read the diff: it is a list of what moved.
